title: Selling options trades away upside: it fits some situations and not others
summary: When you sell an option you sell part of your potential upside. The speaker says this can fit a retiree who wants stability and cash flow with markets at all-time highs. It may not fit someone in their 20s with time on their side, especially after a market drop.

steps.caption: Stock only: you keep all of the upside and all of the downside.
Stock plus a short call: you collect premium, but gains stop at the strike.
The difference is the upside you sold. Above $105 it grows with every dollar.
The premium only lowers your breakeven a little. The downside stays almost the same.
Young investor after a drop: upside matters more. Retiree near highs: cash flow and stability matter more.

takeaways: Selling options sells part of your upside.
It suits investors who want stability and cash flow more than growth.
It may not suit a young investor when markets are off their highs.
caveats: This is general guidance, not personal advice. The clip ends with a follow request.
